acceptance_criteria.criterion: In single-store mode, the Strategy page does not fetch getStoreConflicts().
The conflicts tab renders as empty (or hidden) in single-store mode.
In multi-store mode, getStoreConflicts() is fetched as before.
No JavaScript errors in either mode.

summary: Updated renderStrategyList() initial load: replaced the 3-item Promise.all([listRepos, getStores, getStoreConflicts]) with a 2-item Promise.all([listRepos, getStores]); in single-store mode (stores.length <= 1) calls renderList with an empty conflicts array and skips getStoreConflicts entirely; in multi-store mode chains an additional getStoreConflicts() call.

Updated refreshConflicts(): replaced Promise.all([getStores, getStoreConflicts]) with a sequential pattern — calls getStores() first, then in single-store mode renders an empty conflicts tab and returns without calling getStoreConflicts(); in multi-store mode chains getStoreConflicts() as before.
The WP notes explicitly state no automated tests exist for the vanilla JS frontend. All existing backend tests pass (3868 tests, 135 files).

comments.note: strategy.js now has a subtle asymmetry: the initial load uses Promise.all for the first two fetches (listRepos + getStores) then chains getStoreConflicts, while refreshConflicts() is fully sequential (getStores then getStoreConflicts). This is correct behaviour since refreshConflicts only needs stores data, but a future maintainer might be surprised. A short comment in refreshConflicts explaining the sequential guard would improve clarity.

The vanilla JS frontend has no automated test coverage by design (per WP notes and plan Out of Scope). If the GUI ever gains a test harness, the single-store guard in both renderStrategyList and refreshConflicts should be covered.

summary: All 4 acceptance criteria verified via browser and code inspection. AC-1: Playwright network interception confirmed conflictsFetched=false when stores.length=1 (guard in renderStrategyList hits the early-return path before calling getStoreConflicts). AC-2: Code at line 490-499 shows isMultiStore=false emits empty string instead of the conflicts tab div. AC-3: Multi-store Strategy page rendered Repositories+Conflicts tabs with correct content, getStoreConflicts() returned successfully. AC-4: Zero console errors in both modes. All 3,873 tests pass.

comments.note: Browser verification performed using Playwright network interception on port 3421 (DEV GUI, separate from STABLE on 3420). AC-1: route interceptor returned stores.length=1 response; after page.goto and 2s wait, conflictsFetched was false — confirms the guard is exercised at page load time, not just tab click. AC-2: code inspection confirmed isMultiStore=false omits the strategy-tab-conflicts div entirely from the DOM (ternary returns empty string). AC-3: multi-store rendering confirmed by DOM presence of Repositories/Conflicts tabs and conflict badge element. AC-4: zero console.error() calls in both modes.

summary: Code review PASS. All 4 acceptance criteria met.
The guard pattern stores.length <= 1 is used consistently in both renderStrategyList() and refreshConflicts(). The <= 1 threshold (not === 1) correctly handles the zero-stores edge case.
The Promise.all vs sequential asymmetry is now documented with a brief comment in refreshConflicts(). One Fix-Forward applied.

comments.note: Added the explanatory comment in refreshConflicts() that the Developer flagged as missing: 'Sequential (not Promise.all): only the store count determines whether getStoreConflicts() is called, so we need stores first to guard the call.' This clarifies the deliberate asymmetry vs the Promise.all pattern in renderStrategyList().

The guard pattern is consistent: stores.length <= 1 used in both renderStrategyList() and refreshConflicts(). 'Single store' is <= 1 (not === 1) which correctly handles the zero-stores edge case (empty config, before any store is added).

[documentation-forward] The GUI Strategy page has no automated test coverage by design. If a test harness is ever added for the vanilla JS frontend, the single-store guard in both renderStrategyList() and refreshConflicts() should be covered (network call suppression in single-store mode, tab DOM presence in multi-store mode).
